message:
## Vulnerability Digest

Fresh sweep completed for the daily run using the monitored product list in Products.txt. Several credible, product-matched vulnerability reports were published or updated in the last 24 hours. The highest-priority items are Veeam Backup & Replication RCE, Google Chrome's exploited V8 issue, MongoDB Server CVEs, Adobe Acrobat/Reader critical fixes, OpenSSL's June advisory, and Microsoft's June Patch Tuesday set.

**Finding 1: Veeam Backup & Replication remote code execution**

- Product: Veeam Backup & Replication
- Issue: CVE-2026-44963
- Severity: Critical, CVSS v4 9.4, as stated by Veeam and NVD
- Description: Veeam disclosed a remote code execution vulnerability on the backup server that can be triggered by an authenticated domain user. The vendor states the issue affects Veeam Backup & Replication 12.3.2.4465 and earlier version 12 builds, and only impacts domain-joined backup servers.
- Why it appears relevant: The monitored list includes Veeam.
- Source: Veeam KB4869: https://www.veeam.com/kb4869; NVD: https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-44963

**Finding 2: Google Chrome V8 vulnerability added to CISA KEV**

- Product: Google Chrome
- Issue: CVE-2026-11645
- Severity: High in the Chrome advisory; CISA KEV indicates known exploitation
- Description: Google released Chrome 149.0.7827.102/.103 for Windows and macOS and 149.0.7827.102 for Linux with 74 security fixes. CVE-2026-11645 is an out-of-bounds memory access issue in V8. CISA added it to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog based on evidence of active exploitation.
- Why it appears relevant: The monitored list includes Google Chrome.
- Source: Google Chrome Releases: https://chromereleases.googleblog.com/2026/06/stable-channel-update-for-desktop_0153744567.html; CISA alert: https://www.cisa.gov/news-events/alerts/2026/06/09/cisa-adds-three-known-exploited-vulnerabilities-catalog

**Finding 3: MongoDB Server security CVEs published June 9**

- Product: MongoDB Server
- Issue: CVE-2026-9740 and related MongoDB Server CVEs published in the same advisory batch
- Severity: CVE-2026-9740 score 8.7 on MongoDB's alert page; other same-day MongoDB Server entries range from lower to high scores
- Description: MongoDB listed multiple June 9 security CVEs. The most severe visible item, CVE-2026-9740, is an unbounded recursion issue in BSONColumn interleaved-reference handling that can allow an unauthenticated user to crash MongoDB Server. MongoDB also published multiple additional server crash, memory disclosure, and data exposure CVEs for affected 7.0, 8.0, 8.2, and 8.3 version lines.
- Why it appears relevant: The monitored list includes MongoDB, and the alert explicitly names MongoDB Server.
- Source: MongoDB Alerts: https://www.mongodb.com/resources/products/alerts

**Finding 4: Adobe Acrobat and Reader critical and important vulnerabilities**

- Product: Adobe Acrobat / Acrobat Reader
- Issue: APSB26-63, including CVE-2026-47911 through CVE-2026-47926 and related CVEs listed by Adobe
- Severity: Critical and Important, as stated by Adobe
- Description: Adobe released security updates for Acrobat and Reader on Windows and macOS. The advisory includes multiple arbitrary code execution vulnerabilities, application denial-of-service issues, and memory exposure issues. Adobe says it is not aware of exploitation in the wild for the issues addressed in this update.
- Why it appears relevant: The monitored list includes Adobe Acrobat.
- Source: Adobe APSB26-63: https://helpx.adobe.com/security/products/acrobat/apsb26-63.html

**Finding 5: OpenSSL June 9 security advisory**

- Product: OpenSSL
- Issue: Multiple CVEs, including CVE-2026-45447, CVE-2026-34182, CVE-2026-42764, CVE-2026-45445, CVE-2026-7383, and CVE-2026-9076
- Severity: OpenSSL lists CVE-2026-45447 as High; several others are Moderate or Low
- Description: OpenSSL published a June 9 advisory covering multiple vulnerabilities across OpenSSL 1.0.2, 1.1.1, 3.0, 3.4, 3.5, 3.6, and 4.0 branches. The highest-severity item is a PKCS7_verify() use-after-free that may lead to crashes, heap corruption, or potentially remote code execution in applications processing crafted PKCS#7 or S/MIME signed messages using the affected APIs.
- Why it appears relevant: The monitored list includes OpenSSL.
- Source: OpenSSL vulnerabilities page: https://openssl-library.org/news/vulnerabilities/; oss-sec mirror: https://seclists.org/oss-sec/2026/q2/861

**Finding 6: Microsoft June 2026 Patch Tuesday updates**

- Product: Windows Server / Windows 10 / Microsoft Office / Microsoft .NET / Microsoft Defender / Visual Studio / Visual Studio Code / IIS and related Microsoft components
- Issue: Multiple June 2026 Microsoft CVEs, including Windows, Office, .NET, Visual Studio Code, Remote Desktop, DHCP Client, HTTP.sys, and IIS-relevant issues
- Severity: Mixed Critical and Important; Microsoft was not aware of exploitation in the wild for the Patch Tuesday set according to Rapid7's summary
- Description: Microsoft released a large June security update set. Rapid7 notes roughly 200 Microsoft vulnerabilities in the June Patch Tuesday release, including multiple public disclosures but no known in-the-wild exploitation at publication time. The release includes items relevant to monitored Microsoft products and server components, including Windows, Office, .NET, Visual Studio/VS Code, Remote Desktop, DHCP Client, HTTP.sys, and IIS-adjacent web server exposure.
- Why it appears relevant: The monitored list includes Windows Server 2012 R2, Windows 10, Microsoft Office, Microsoft Edge, Microsoft .NET, Windows Defender, Visual Studio, Visual Studio Code, IIS, PowerShell, and Azure DevOps/TFS.
- Source: Microsoft Security Update Guide June 2026: https://msrc.microsoft.com/update-guide/releaseNote/2026-Jun; Rapid7 Patch Tuesday summary: https://www.rapid7.com/blog/post/em-patch-tuesday-june-2026/; Cisco Talos summary: https://blog.talosintelligence.com/microsoft-patch-tuesday-for-june-2026-snort-rules-and-prominent-vulnerabilities/

**Possible matches needing review**

- Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager / Controller / Validator CVE-2026-20245 was added to CISA KEV and is being actively exploited, but it does not clearly match the monitored Cisco entries, which are Cisco Nexus, Cisco UCS, and Cisco Fabric Extender. I excluded it from confirmed findings for this run. Source: https://www.cisa.gov/news-events/alerts/2026/06/09/cisa-adds-three-known-exploited-vulnerabilities-catalog
- HTTP/2 Bomb / CVE-2026-49975 affects Apache HTTP Server and is discussed as affecting other major HTTP/2 server implementations. It was originally disclosed before this 24-hour window, so it is not counted as a fresh confirmed finding today, but it remains relevant to Apache HTTP Server, Nginx, and IIS exposure reviews. Source: https://httpd.apache.org/security/vulnerabilities_24.html

Closing note: Immediate review is recommended for domain-joined Veeam Backup & Replication 12 servers, Chrome deployments, MongoDB Server 7.0/8.x fleets, Acrobat/Reader installations, and OpenSSL consumers that process PKCS#7 or S/MIME data. Microsoft Patch Tuesday coverage should be handled through the normal emergency/expedited patch triage process, prioritizing exposed servers and components with Critical RCE or higher exploitation likelihood.
